subject.title: Redondo Beach — Measure ART (Commercial Development and Housing Density Land-Use)

text: Shall the measure be adopted to amend the Redondo Beach General Plan and Zoning Ordinance to support increased commercial activity in key areas of the City, including expanded property development potential (i.e. new floor area ratio caps, height limits, and rooftop dining) along Artesia and Aviation Boulevards, industrial properties north of Manhattan Beach Boulevard, and certain commercial properties along Pacific Coast Highway; and to reduce the allowed housing density for some residential and mixed-use properties in the City?
Redondo Beach City Council and Mayor

analysis.title: City Attorney's Impartial Analysis of Measure Art

text: The City of Redondo Beach's development regulations are contained in its General Plan, Zoning, Coastal Land Use Plan, and Coastal Zoning ("Plan(s)"). These Plans regulate land use, residential density (dwelling units/acre [du/acre]), and building intensity (e.g. floor area ratio [FAR]: the total building floor area divided by the total land area).

The State of California recommends updates to these Plans at least once every 20 years. While the City has previously approved Plan amendments, the Plans were last substantially updated in 1992. Consequently, in 2016, the City initiated a Plan update, which received input from the City's elected officials, the City's Planners/Commissions, and community members, including residents in the General Plan Advisory Committee. This process culminated in the City Council's adoption of Plan amendments in 2024 and 2026. However, before the Plan amendments become effective, City Charter Article XXVII requires a public vote, which was consolidated with the statewide general election.
Measure ART was placed on the ballot by the City Council, and would amend the City's Plans. The amendments are in Sections 3 and 4.

Section 3 of the Measure amends the Plans along Artesia Boulevard, the Galleria Mall, Torrance Boulevard, Pacific Coast Highway, and certain coastal areas. These amendments (a) convert some properties from mixed-use and residential to commercial zoning, (b) reduce residential density in some areas from 35 to 30 du/acre, (c) increase residential density in other areas from 28 to 30 du/acre, (d) create a Mixed-Use Transit Center zone, and (e) establish an Industrial Flex overlay zone, which allows light industrial and commercial uses, including research and development, technology/incubator spaces, offices, and hotels, at a maximum FAR of 1.0.

Section 4 of the Measure also includes Plan amendments to industrial areas north of Manhattan Beach Boulevard, commercial areas along Artesia and Aviation Boulevards, and areas along Pacific Coast Highway. For areas north of Manhattan Beach Boulevard, the Measure increases the maximum FAR from 0.7 to 1.0. For areas along Artesia and Aviation Boulevards, the Measure (a) redesignates some areas to a Neighborhood Commercial zone, (b) increases the maximum FAR from 0.6 to 1.5, (c) increases maximum building height from 30 to 45 feet, (d) increases development potential from two to three stories, and (e) establishes pedestrian-oriented architectural and design standards. For areas along Pacific Coast Highway, the Measure changes some areas to a Commercial C-4 zone, which increases the maximum FAR from 0.5 to 1.0.

As required by Article XXVII, the City has produced descriptions, maps, and technical analyses of the proposed changes. Information is available to the public on the City's website at https://www.redondo.org/ArticleXXVII.

The Measure requires approval by a majority of the voters in the City to become effective. A "yes" vote favors the changes, and a "no" vote opposes them. The Plan amendments in the Coastal Zone also need Coastal Commission approval to become effective. The Measure does not include amendments related to Public Institutional zones, such as school property, the Civic Center, and Beach Cities Health District property.

The above statement is an impartial analysis of Measure ART. If you desire a copy of the measure, please call the elections official's office at (310)318-0656 and a copy will be mailed at no cost to you. Information regarding Measure ART may be obtained by visiting Redondo.org/elections.
